info.name: University LMS — API v1
info.description:
REST API for the University LMS modular monolith.

## Start

All commands run from `UniPro-Backend/`.

```
docker compose up -d
./mvnw spring-boot:run
```

That is the whole setup. **No SQL seeding is required** — folder `01 · Reference data` creates the users, faculty, department, programme, academic year and term through the API, and captures every id into a collection variable for the folders that follow.

## Order

Run the folders top to bottom, or use the Collection Runner. Two orderings are real constraints rather than convention:

- A course is created **DRAFT** and must be **ACTIVE** before a section can be added.
- A section is created **PLANNED** and must be **OPEN**, *and* the term's registration window must be open, before anyone can enrol.

Codes, usernames and student numbers are randomised by pre-request scripts, so the collection is re-runnable without tripping unique indexes.

## Authentication

There is none yet — `/api/v1/**` is `permitAll()`. That is a scaffolding decision and a deployment blocker, tracked as ROADMAP P0.1. When JWT lands, set a bearer token at collection level and every request inherits it.

item.name: 01 · Reference data (run first)
item.description:
Builds the academic structure a course needs, entirely through the API.

A course belongs to a **department**, a section is scheduled in an **academic term**, and a student is admitted to a **programme** — so none of those can be created until this folder has run. Every id is captured into a collection variable, so later folders just work.

Run top to bottom once against a fresh database. Codes are randomised per run so the folder can be re-run without tripping the unique indexes.

request.description: Accounts are created **PENDING_ACTIVATION** — existing is not the same as being allowed to sign in. Note the response has no password field: the hash is never serialised.
Provisioning and enabling access are separate events, so each is independently auditable.
Roles are rows, not an enum, so the set can change without a redeploy. The six standard roles are installed by V14__seed_reference_data.sql.

Top of the hierarchy. Codes are normalised to upper case on the way in — otherwise 'comp' and 'COMP' would both satisfy the unique index and become two departments every human reader would call the same one.
**This is what a course needs.** `departmentId` from here is the field that was previously impossible to obtain without SQL.
A student is admitted to a programme; `programmeId` is required to create one.
A session such as 2026/2027. `endDate` must be after `startDate`; the service checks it so the error names the field, rather than surfacing as a generic constraint violation.

A section is scheduled in a term. Created **closed to registration** — a term with no window does not accept enrolment. That is deliberate: registration has to be opened, not left open because a field was never set.

Opens enrolment from yesterday to 90 days out, computed by a pre-request script so the window is always live when you run it.

Without this, enrolment is refused with 422 ENROLLMENT_REGISTRATION_CLOSED. PUT because it replaces the window wholesale and repeating it leaves the term in the same state.
Paged, like every collection endpoint.
Optional facultyId filter.
Not paged: a year holds a handful of terms, bounded by the calendar.
Single faculty.
Single department. `id` here is what a course's `departmentId` must be.
Single programme. `id` here is what a student's `programmeId` must be.
Paged; optional departmentId filter.
Paged, newest first.
Single year.
Single term. `registrationOpen` is evaluated server-side at request time — the term owns that rule rather than leaving the client to derive it from two timestamps.
Paged. No password hash appears in any representation.
Single account.
Role names currently held. Fetch-joined server-side, so this is one query, not one per grant.

item.name: 04 · Enrollments
item.description: The concurrency-critical path. Requires an OPEN section (folder 02), an ACTIVE student (folder 03) and an open registration window (folder 01).

request.description:
The seat is taken by one guarded UPDATE
  (SET enrolled_count = enrolled_count + 1 WHERE id = ? AND enrolled_count < capacity)
so two simultaneous callers are serialised by the database and exactly one wins. The seat and the enrolment row commit together: if the insert fails, the rollback returns the seat.

Same student, same section. The service checks first for a good message, but the unique index on (student_id, course_section_id) is the actual guarantee — it is what rejects the loser when two identical requests arrive at once.
enrolledCount is the counter the guarded UPDATE maintains; a CHECK constraint keeps it inside 0..capacity regardless of how it is written.
Single record.
Filter by student, section or status.

ENROLLED -> DROPPED, seat returned.

Lifecycle changes are named actions rather than a PATCH taking a status: dropping and withdrawing differ academically, and an endpoint accepting an arbitrary target would invite transitions the domain forbids. DROPPED is terminal — run it twice and the second gets 422.
Leaving after the drop window — recorded on the transcript, seat still released. Run on a fresh enrolment; after a drop this correctly returns 422.

exec: pm.test('200 if fresh, 422 if already terminal', () =>

item.name: 05 · Error contract
item.description: Every failure returns the same envelope: timestamp, status, code, message, path, traceId, errors[]. Clients branch on `code`, never on prose. Stack traces, SQL and constraint names never appear — they go to the log under the same traceId.

request.description: Empty body. One entry per rejected field, with the rejected value — except where the field name looks like a secret, which is redacted.
A too-short password. The rule is reported, but the value is **not** reflected into the response body or the access log — the field name is recognised as sensitive.
Referential checks happen in the service, so the error names the missing thing rather than surfacing as a foreign-key violation.
endDate before startDate. Checked in the service so the message is actionable; a CHECK constraint also exists to stop bad data arriving by any other route.
Unparseable body. The parser's message can quote the payload, so it is logged and never returned.
Well-formed but unknown UUID; module-owned code.
Type mismatch on a path variable, handled as a 400 rather than a 500.
Re-sends the code created in folder 02.
No DELETE on a course: catalog entries are retired, never removed, so historical results stay interpretable.
